title: The Sister's Price
next_chapter_hook: The token glowed faintly in Chen Nian's palm, as if calling out to something. Chen Ji knew that the next truth was about to be revealed—and the price might be even heavier than three years of feigning death.

text.content: As the mist cleared, a face hauntingly familiar appeared before Chen Ji. Those eyes—phoenix eyes identical to his own, now veiled in a maturity unfitting a young girl. At her temples, three stark white strands of hair had appeared.

dialogue.content: Brother, it's me. Nian'er has returned.

text.content: Chen Ji felt his heart skip a beat. For three years, he had seen this face countless times in dreams, yet never imagined a reunion in such circumstances. He wanted to reach out and touch it, but froze mid-gesture—for he noticed the faint, almost imperceptible formation rune between Chen Nian's brows.

dialogue.content: Are you looking at this?" Chen Nian touched the rune between her brows, a bitter smile crossing her face, "It's just the price of the feigning death formation. It doesn't hurt, truly."

text.content: Doesn't hurt? Chen Ji felt his chest being gripped tightly. Three strands of white hair, three years of life—this was the price his sister, whom he had tried so desperately to protect, had paid for him. He suddenly recalled that strange light during Volume Five, realizing that at that very moment, Nian'er had been bearing something for him.

dialogue.content: Brother, don't blame yourself." Chen Nian gently grasped his rigid hand, her palm ice-cold, "When I discovered the feigning death formation in the Holy Sect's secret chamber, I knew this was my only chance to help you. The formation requires the caster to use their lifespan as a catalyst—

text.content: You traded your life for mine?" Chen Ji's voice turned hoarse, his knuckles white from gripping. He would rather face the encirclement of three great sects, would rather becalculating by the Eyes of Heaven, than see his sister sacrifice even a fraction of herself for him.

dialogue.content: Brother, listen to me." Chen Nian's tone suddenly turned serious, "In that secret chamber, I didn't just activate the feigning death formation. I also... resonated with the Tianji Record's true body."

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. The Tianji Record's true body? Isn't that—He lowered his gaze to the faint fragment mark on his palm, his heart surging with tremendous waves. Could it be that Nian'er also carries a part of the Tianji Record?

dialogue.content: In that moment of resonance, I saw many things." Chen Nian's voice became ethereal, "But the price was... my memories of that time became very vague. I only remember a few key fragments."

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the churning emotions within him. Remembering grudges without acting rashly—this had always been his principle. Nian'er's sacrifice was already a fact; what mattered most now was to excavate useful information from her remaining memories.

dialogue.content: Nian'er, do you still remember—" Chen Ji carefully chose his words, "About Mother? Did she leave anything behind? Any clues pointing to a specific location?

text.content: Chen Nian closed her eyes, her brow furrowing tightly. A moment later, she opened them, a glimmer of light flickering in her gaze: "Tianji Pavilion... headquarters. I remember these words. And there's something else—Mother said only Chen bloodline can activate it."

choice.prompt: Chen Nian retrieved an antique jade pendant from her怀, the pendant's center carved with a unique Chen family符文, now emanating a faint glow. Chen Ji's heart tightened—this aura was strikingly similar to the Tianji Record Fragment.

choices.description: This might be the last clue Mother left behind; must immediately confirm its authenticity and purpose.

text.content: Chen Ji took the jade pendant, and a warmth so achingly familiar instantly spread through his palm. The符文 seemed to be calling out to something, resonating with some dormant power within his bloodline.

choices.description: No token is more important than Nian'er's wellbeing. He needed to confirm his sister's true condition.

dialogue.content: Brother..." Chen Nian's eyes reddened slightly, "I'm really fine. Don't worry about me.

choices.description: What exactly did the Holy Sect do to Nian'er? His fury needed an outlet.
choices.risk_hint: Exposing Hostility Toward the Holy Sect

dialogue.content: Brother, don't ask anymore." Chen Nian gently shook her head, "Those people don't matter. What matters is that we're together now.

text.content: Chen Ji tucked the jade pendant into his sleeve, already calculating in his heart. Regardless of whether the Tianji Pavilion headquarters was a dragon's den or a tiger's lair, he had to make this journey. But before that, there was something even more important he needed to do—making amends for these three years of separation from his sister.

dialogue.content: Brother, why are you smiling?" Chen Nian gazed at the faint smile at the corner of Chen Ji's lips, a sense of unease rising within her. She knew her brother too well—whenever he wore such an expression, it meant someone was about to suffer.

text.content: Nothing." Chen Ji shook his head, though his gaze turned deep and dangerous, "Just thinking that what the Holy Sect owes us, one day we'll claim with interest. But for now, Nian'er, rest well. I'll handle the Tianji Pavilion matter."

dialogue.content: Chen Nian was silent for a moment, then suddenly retrieved the jade pendant from her sleeve, holding it before Chen Ji. The符文 at the pendant's center emitted a ghostly glow, as if awaiting the moment of awakening. "Mother said only Chen bloodline can activate this. Brother, try it."

text.content: Chen Ji took the jade pendant, and the instant his fingertip touched the符文, a warmth so achingly familiar spread throughout his entire body. That sensation was identical to when he first obtained the Tianji Record Fragment—yet it carried an additional strand of bloodline kinship. He raised his head to look at Chen Nian, seeing the expectant gleam in his sister's eyes. Three years of separation, the price of feigning death, the haziness of memories... all of this pointed toward an answer. Chen Ji took a deep breath, gripping the jade pendant tightly in his palm.
